title: OSHA construction scaffolds practice questions
description: Free practice questions on OSHA scaffold rules (29 CFR 1926 Subpart L). Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Each scaffold and scaffold component (outside the listed exceptions) must support its own weight plus at least how many times the maximum intended load?
questions.explanation: The rule says each scaffold and component "shall be capable of supporting, without failure, its own weight and at least 4 times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to it."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: its own weight and at least 4 times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to it

questions.question: Each suspension rope on a non-adjustable suspension scaffold, including connecting hardware, must support at least how many times the maximum intended load applied to that rope?
questions.explanation: Each such rope "shall be capable of supporting, without failure, at least 6 times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to that rope."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: used on non-adjustable suspension scaffolds shall be capable of supporting, without failure, at least 6 times the maximum intended load

questions.question: Who must design a scaffold?

options.A: Any employee who will work on it

questions.explanation: "Scaffolds shall be designed by a qualified person and shall be constructed and loaded in accordance with that design."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Scaffolds shall be designed by a qualified person and shall be constructed and loaded in accordance with that design.

questions.question: Which two things together make someone a competent person under Subpart L?

options.A: A college degree and ten years of experience
options.B: Ownership of the scaffold and a state license
options.C: Membership in a union and a first aid card
options.D: The ability to identify existing and predictable hazards, and authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them

questions.explanation: A competent person is "capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards" and "has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.450, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

questions.question: Unless the employer can show a wider space is necessary, what is the widest gap allowed between adjacent platform units on a fully planked platform?
questions.explanation: Platform units must be installed so the space between adjacent units and between the platform and the uprights "is no more than 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, except where the employer can demonstrate that a wider space is necessary."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: is no more than 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, except where the employer can demonstrate that a wider space is necessary

questions.question: Apart from the listed exceptions, what is the minimum width of each scaffold platform and walkway?
questions.explanation: Except as provided in (b)(2)(i) and (ii), "each scaffold platform and walkway shall be at least 18 inches (46 cm) wide."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: each scaffold platform and walkway shall be at least 18 inches (46 cm) wide.

questions.question: Unless the platform end is cleated or otherwise restrained by hooks or equivalent means, how far must each end extend over the centerline of its support?
questions.explanation: Each end of a platform, unless cleated or restrained, "shall extend over the centerline of its support at least 6 inches (15 cm)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall extend over the centerline of its support at least 6 inches (15 cm).

questions.question: A supported scaffold must be restrained from tipping by guying, tying, bracing or equivalent means when its height to base width ratio is more than what?
questions.explanation: Supported scaffolds with a height to base width ratio "of more than four to one (4:1) shall be restrained from tipping by guying, tying, bracing, or equivalent means."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: ratio of more than four to one (4:1) shall be restrained from tipping by guying, tying, bracing, or equivalent means

questions.question: What must the poles, legs, posts, frames and uprights of a supported scaffold bear on?

options.A: Unstable objects, if they are level
options.C: Base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation

questions.explanation: They "shall bear on base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation," and unstable objects may not be used to support scaffolds.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall bear on base plates and mud sills or other adequate firm foundation.

questions.question: A means of access such as a ladder, stair tower or ramp must be used when a scaffold platform is more than how far above or below a point of access?
questions.explanation: Access must be provided "when scaffold platforms are more than 2 feet (0.6 m) above or below a point of access," and crossbraces may not be used as access.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When scaffold platforms are more than 2 feet (0.6 m) above or below a point of access

questions.question: When is crossbracing acceptable in place of a midrail?

options.A: When the crossing point of two braces is between 20 and 30 inches above the work platform
options.B: At any height, as long as the braces are steel
options.C: When the crossing point is more than 48 inches above the work platform
options.D: When the braces are also used as the means of access

questions.explanation: Crossbracing may replace a midrail "when the crossing point of two braces is between 20 inches (0.5 m) and 30 inches (0.8 m) above the work platform." Separately, "Crossbraces shall not be used as a means of access."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Crossbracing is acceptable in place of a midrail when the crossing point of two braces is between 20 inches (0.5 m) and 30 inches (0.8 m) above the work platform

questions.question: How high above the scaffold supporting level may the bottom rung of a hook-on or attachable ladder be?
questions.explanation: Hook-on and attachable ladders must be positioned "so that their bottom rung is not more than 24 inches (61 cm) above the scaffold supporting level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: so that their bottom rung is not more than 24 inches (61 cm) above the scaffold supporting level

questions.question: When must a competent person inspect scaffolds and scaffold components for visible defects?

options.A: Before each work shift, and after any occurrence which could affect structural integrity
options.C: Only when the scaffold is first erected

questions.explanation: Scaffolds "shall be inspected for visible defects by a competent person before each work shift, and after any occurrence which could affect a scaffold's structural integrity."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall be inspected for visible defects by a competent person before each work shift, and after any occurrence which could affect a scaffold's structural integrity.

questions.question: Under whose supervision and direction may scaffolds be erected, moved, dismantled or altered?

options.B: A competent person qualified in scaffold erection, moving, dismantling or alteration

questions.explanation: These activities may happen "only under the supervision and direction of a competent person qualified in scaffold erection, moving, dismantling or alteration."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: only under the supervision and direction of a competent person qualified in scaffold erection, moving, dismantling or alteration.

questions.question: What minimum clearance does the rule set between a scaffold and an exposed, energized, uninsulated power line of less than 50 kV (without the utility exception)?
questions.explanation: For uninsulated lines under 50 kV the table sets a minimum distance of "10 feet (3.1 m)"; closer work needs the utility or system operator to have deenergized, relocated or covered the lines.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Uninsulated lines voltage Minimum distance Less than 50 kv 10 feet (3.1 m)

questions.question: Above what height must each employee on a scaffold be protected from falling to a lower level?
questions.explanation: "Each employee on a scaffold more than 10 feet (3.1 m) above a lower level shall be protected from falling to that lower level."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each employee on a scaffold more than 10 feet (3.1 m) above a lower level shall be protected from falling to that lower level.

questions.question: What fall protection is required for each employee on a single-point or two-point adjustable suspension scaffold?

options.A: Both a personal fall arrest system and a guardrail system

questions.explanation: Each such employee "shall be protected by both a personal fall arrest system and guardrail system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each employee on a single-point or two-point adjustable suspension scaffold shall be protected by both a personal fall arrest system and guardrail system

questions.question: On a supported scaffold manufactured or placed in service after January 1, 2000, where must the top edge of the toprail be?

options.A: Between 30 and 34 inches above the platform
options.B: Between 38 and 45 inches above the platform
options.C: Between 20 and 26 inches above the platform
options.D: Between 12 and 18 inches above the platform

questions.explanation: On those scaffolds the top edge "shall be installed between 38 inches (0.97 m) and 45 inches (1.2 m) above the platform surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall be installed between 38 inches (0.97 m) and 45 inches (1.2 m) above the platform surface.

questions.question: Where used on a scaffold, how high must a toeboard be, measured from its top edge to the walking/working surface?

options.C: At least three and one-half inches

questions.explanation: Toeboards must be "at least three and one-half inches (9 cm) high from the top edge of the toeboard to the level of the walking/working surface."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.451, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: At least three and one-half inches (9 cm) high from the top edge of the toeboard to the level of the walking/working surface.

questions.question: Who must train each employee involved in erecting, disassembling, moving, operating, repairing, maintaining or inspecting a scaffold?
questions.explanation: The employer must have each such employee "trained by a competent person to recognize any hazards associated with the work in question."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.454, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: trained by a competent person to recognize any hazards associated with the work in question.
